audit.whatIsWrong: Eternal Hunger was described three times as healing him 'harder the lower your HP gets'.
audit.why: Riot's text keys the passive to WARWICK's own health — he heals the bonus damage when he is below 50%, and triples it below 25%. Written the old way, you are told that hurting him is what feeds him, when in fact keeping him above 50% is the goal and shoving him low is what turns his sustain on.
audit.corrected: Passive now stated as his own sub-50% and sub-25% thresholds in the level 1-3 spike, early text and whys[0] and whys[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: Every spike was gated on Infinite Duress with no cooldown, and Primal Howl was absent from the entire entry.
audit.why: Infinite Duress is 110/90/70 — at rank 1 that is a window you can plan a whole lane around. Primal Howl at 15/14/13/12/11 gives 2.5 seconds of damage reduction and then fears you, which is exactly what eats the front of an Akali burst and pushes you out mid-combo.
audit.corrected: Infinite Duress at 110s rank 1 added to the cooldown block and phases; Primal Howl added to the level 6 spike, the late text and the cooldown block.

audit.whatIsWrong: Infinite Duress was called 'point-and-click' in four places, and the full layer told you to 'W-shroud his R suppress' while the content layer correctly said Shroud cannot break a suppression.
audit.why: Infinite Duress is a leap in a direction that suppresses the first champion it COLLIDES with. Because it is collision-based rather than targeted, being unselectable inside Twilight Shroud does not stop it — the two layers were giving opposite advice about the most lethal ability in the lane.
audit.corrected: All point-and-click references replaced with the directional collision leap, and the full layer's shroud-dodge instruction rewritten to agree with the content layer.

edits.before: Warwick's passive heals harder the lower your HP, so every auto trade refills him; his Q heals on hit and Blood Hunt move speed (triggered when you drop below 50%) lets him walk you down before you even have Twilight Shroud at 2.
edits.after: Warwick's passive heals him harder the lower HIS OWN health is — below 50%, tripled below 25% — so a losing trade refills him; Jaws of the Beast heals on hit and Blood Hunt speed walks him at you before you have Shroud at 2.

edits.before: Your one clean kill window: bait or wait out his Infinite Duress channel, then E-flip onto him and chain both casts of Perfect Execution to execute before his drain heal out-paces your burst.
edits.after: Your one clean kill window: bait Primal Howl and wait out Infinite Duress — a directional leap, not a click — then E-flip onto him and chain both Perfect Execution casts before his drain out-paces you.

edits.before: His biggest threat window: Blood Hunt's low-HP detection and chase plus a point-and-click Infinite Duress suppress yank you out of Shroud and delete you in any skirmish, while his drain heals through your single combo.
edits.after: His biggest threat window: Blood Hunt's low-HP chase plus an Infinite Duress leap that suppresses the first champion it collides with, while Primal Howl's damage reduction blunts the burst you open with.

edits.before: Hold your R and burst until his Infinite Duress is down, then E-flip in and chain both Perfect Execution casts to execute him
edits.after: Hold your R until Infinite Duress is down, then E-flip in and chain both Perfect Execution casts to execute him inside that window

edits.before: Drop Twilight Shroud to go untargetable and break his Blood Hunt chase, then reset the trade from the smoke — never facetank inside it
edits.after: Drop Twilight Shroud to break his chase, but never lean on it against Infinite Duress — that leap collides with you, it does not target you

edits.before: Land Infinite Duress to suppress you out of Shroud and lock you through your R channel
edits.after: Leap Infinite Duress into you for the suppress, then Primal Howl to fear you off him

edits.before: Drag fights long so his low-HP passive heal and Q drain out-sustain your one burst rotation
edits.after: Drag fights long so his sub-50% passive heal and Q drain out-sustain your one rotation

edits.before: Warwick owns these levels — his passive heals harder the lower your HP gets, so trading autos just feeds his sustain, and his Q heal plus Blood Hunt move speed (which procs the moment you drop under 50% HP) lets him walk you down before you even have Twilight Shroud at level 2. Last-hit at max kunai range and do not get greedy, because once Blood Hunt is active there is no Q max-range slow that stops a move-speed bruiser already on top of you. Concede CS, eat minimal poke, and wait for your spike.
edits.after: Warwick owns these levels — his passive heals him whenever HE is below 50% health and triples it below 25%, so shoving him low is what switches his sustain on, and his Q heal plus Blood Hunt move speed (which procs the moment YOU drop under 50%) lets him walk you down before you even have Twilight Shroud at level 2. Last-hit at max kunai range and do not get greedy, because once Blood Hunt is active no max-range Q slow stops a move-speed bruiser already on top of you. Concede CS and wait for your spike.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 even out once you have all three basics — Shroud lets you go untargetable and reset, and your Assassin's Mark empowered auto punishes a greedy step-up — but the real swing is 6. Your R is the answer: bait his Infinite Duress or simply wait until it is down, then E-flip onto him and chain both casts of Perfect Execution to execute before his drain heal catches up. Never commit into an up R — his point-and-click suppress channels you in place and yanks you out of your own ult mid-cast, and Shroud cannot break a suppression.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 even out once you have all three basics — Shroud lets you go unselectable and reset, and your Assassin's Mark empowered attack punishes a greedy step-up — but the real swing is 6. Your R is the answer: wait until Infinite Duress is down, 110s at rank 1, then E-flip onto him and chain both casts of Perfect Execution to execute before his drain heal catches up. Never commit into an up R — that leap suppresses the first champion it collides with, and no amount of Shroud breaks a suppression.

edits.before: Late game flips back to Warwick hard. His Blood Hunt gives a long low-HP detection-and-chase window that re-acquires you even after a Shroud reposition, and his point-and-click Infinite Duress suppresses you through any escape attempt while his drain heals through your one combo. Your single-target magic burst cannot out-DPS a fed drain bruiser, so you must convert your level-6-to-Lich-Bane lead into a closed lane and side-step his suppress in every teamfight.
edits.after: Late game flips back to Warwick hard. Blood Hunt gives a long low-HP detection-and-chase window that re-acquires you even after a Shroud reposition, Infinite Duress suppresses on collision so unselectable does not save you, and Primal Howl gives 2.5s of damage reduction into a fear that pushes you out of your own combo. Your single-target magic burst cannot out-DPS a fed drain bruiser, so convert your level-6-to-Lich-Bane lead into a closed lane.

edits.before: His passive heals more the lower your HP, and Blood Hunt move speed sticks him to you before Shroud is even online at 2.
edits.after: His passive heals him more the lower HIS health falls, and Blood Hunt speed sticks him to you before Shroud exists at 2.

edits.before: Still no Shroud at his command and his low-HP heal out-values your level-1 kunai poke every exchange.
edits.after: Still no Shroud, and his sub-50% self-heal out-values your level-1 kunai poke in every exchange.

edits.before: Your R is a gap-close execute — bait or wait out his Infinite Duress, then E-flip in and chain both casts before his heal catches up.
edits.after: Your R is a gap-close execute — wait out his Infinite Duress at 110s, then E-flip in and chain both casts before his heal catches up.

edits.before: Blood Hunt low-HP detection and point-and-click R suppress out-chase your E-flip and out-sustain your single burst once he scales.
edits.after: Blood Hunt chase and a collision-based Infinite Duress leap out-chase your E-flip and out-sustain your single burst once he scales.

edits.before: Shroud his R — anti-heal, Q-poke him. Akali wins the Infinite Duress cooldown windows.
edits.after: Anti-heal him — his R leaps, it never targets. Akali wins the Infinite Duress gaps.

edits.before: Shroud rewrites any trade he starts. Only take the trade when Warwick's Infinite Duress is down.
edits.after: Shroud rewrites any trade he starts. Take it when Infinite Duress is down, 110s at rank 1.

edits.before: - Warwick Infinite Duress: matchup-defining — His all-in suppress. Shroud-dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Warwick Infinite Duress, 110s at rank 1: matchup-defining — a directional leap that suppresses on collision, so Shroud will not save you. - Primal Howl, 15s: damage reduction into a fear. - Your ultimate: kill windows only.

edits.before: His all-in suppress. Shroud-dodge it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: A directional leap that suppresses on collision — shroud won't save you.

notes: Three real errors: Eternal Hunger keys off Warwick's own health, not yours (the old text had it backwards, which reverses your trading plan); Infinite Duress is a directional collision leap, not point-and-click; and the two layers gave opposite advice about whether Twilight Shroud answers it — full said 'W-shroud his R suppress', content said shroud cannot break a suppression. Primal Howl, his 15s damage-reduction-into-fear, did not appear anywhere in the entry despite being the ability that most reliably ruins an Akali all-in.
